page: Amazon Web Services g5g.metal is a bare-metal accelerated compute instance built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It features a dedicated 64-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per physical core. The hardware configuration integrates 128 GB of DDR4 system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Graphics and machine learning acceleration are delivered via two NVIDIA T4G Turing GPUs with a combined 32 GB of video memory. The platform includes a 25 Gbps baseline network interface and provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark data reflects strong multi-threaded and memory-bound performance, led by multi-core stress testing and software compilation under Clang. The system demonstrates exceptional throughput in cached memory reads reaching 3,787.58 GB/sec and high transactional efficiency in Redis set operations at 74.22 million operations per second. In addition, static web serving throughput measures 47.54 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread compute metrics such as single-core Geekbench and compression tasks place lower in relative benchmarks. Large-scale language model generation speeds are also constrained, reflecting the memory bandwidth limits of the T4G accelerator class when running extensive parameter weights.

The absence of local NVMe storage and modest single-core execution speed represent notable architecture tradeoffs. However, eliminating hypervisor overhead via bare-metal access provides predictable hardware execution for specialized operations. The g5g.metal instance is well matched for Arm-native Android cloud streaming, real-time media encoding, computer vision inference, static content distribution, and parallel software build pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services g5g.metal is a bare-metal instance powered by a 64-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture. It is equipped with 128 GB of DDR4 system memory, providing 2 GB per core, and incorporates two NVIDIA T4G GPUs with 32 GB of total VRAM. Network throughput is rated at 25 Gbps baseline, while no local disk storage is included. Benchmark evaluations indicate robust multi-core compute capability, with strong results in parallel tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and high-volume Redis operations exceeding 74 million operations per second. However, single-core throughput and large-scale language model generation remain modest due to single-thread frequency bounds and Turing architecture limitations. This hardware balance suits Arm-native graphics rendering, Android gaming emulation, video encoding, microservices, and targeted machine learning inference workloads requiring dedicated hardware execution without hypervisor overhead.
